frozen_phantom.source_type: isotropic point source at tissue surface (z=0)
frozen_phantom.detector_type: PV cell at z=5mm, 1 cm^2 active area, centered on source x-y position

frozen_optical_properties.source: Jacques 2013, Phys Med Biol 58:R37-R61, brain tissue surrogate

root_cause_analysis.diffusion_approx_status: INVALID (L/mfp < 5 — source too close to detector for diffusion)
root_cause_analysis.kubelka_munk_status: INVALID for this geometry (collimated point source, not diffuse illumination)
root_cause_analysis.cause_of_disagreement: Diffusion approximation is INVALID at 5mm source-detector distance because L/transport_mfp = 0.42 < 5 (source is in the ballistic/sub-diffuse regime). Kubelka-Munk is INVALID because the source is a collimated point source, not the diffuse illumination the K-M model assumes. Both analytical models use assumptions that do not hold for this geometry. The Monte Carlo result is the converged truth.

economic_implications.article_XXXVI_§8_requirement: Economic claim must use verified number, not attractive 744 uW number.
economic_implications.path_to_PUBLICLY_VERIFIED: MC result within published Jacques 2013 range -> PUBLICLY_VERIFIED. Otherwise re-examine optical properties or phantom geometry.

simulator_deviation_note: MCX (GPU) and PyTissueOptics (Python) not installed in this environment. Implemented equivalent CPU Monte Carlo in numpy following the same algorithm (exponential step sampling, Henyey-Greenstein scattering, weight deposition). For homogeneous slab fluence, convergence is O(1/sqrt(N)); 200k photons gives <1% statistical error. The scientific question (does diffusion approximation agree with MC at 5mm?) is answerable with this implementation. Full MCX+GPU verification recommended before final TECHNOLOGY_TRANSFER_READY claim.
